title: Best Hotels in Edinburgh with a Pool: Where to Stay for Comfort and Luxury
excerpt: Finding a hotel with a pool in Edinburgh is rare, but these top-tier properties deliver both swimming facilities and authentic Scottish hospitality. Discover which hotels offer the best poolside experiences without breaking the bank.
content:
## Why Pool Access Matters in Edinburgh

Edinburgh's unpredictable weather makes a quality indoor pool more than just a luxury—it's practical. After spending hours exploring the Royal Mile or hiking Arthur's Seat, a heated pool offers genuine relaxation. Most Edinburgh hotels skip pools entirely, which means the few that offer them stand out significantly. Whether you're traveling with family, visiting for business, or simply want a proper leisure facility, these recommendations deliver what mainstream Edinburgh accommodations avoid.

## The Premium Options

**Prestonfield House Hotel** remains Edinburgh's most luxurious choice for pool access. Located south of the city center in the Prestonfield area, this five-star property features a stunning indoor pool within its leisure complex, alongside a spa and fitness center. Expect to pay $250-400 per night, but you're paying for baroque opulence, impeccable service, and genuine comfort. The location sits near the Meadows and is walkable to Holyrood Palace, though you'll likely want to use their car service or take a short taxi ride to central attractions.

**Murrayfield House Hotel**, nestled in the Murrayfield neighborhood near the rugby stadium, offers mid-range luxury at $150-280 per night. Their heated indoor pool is smaller than Prestonfield's but perfectly functional, and the area feels genuinely local rather than touristy. The neighborhood has solid restaurants and pubs, plus easy bus access to the city center. This works well if you want pool access without paying five-star prices.

## Smart Mid-Range Choices

**Premier Inn Edinburgh City Centre** technically offers pool access through partnership with nearby leisure facilities rather than an on-site pool. At $80-140 per night, it's affordable and central (located on Bread Street), but you'll need to travel separately for swimming. Book early—this property fills quickly.

If you're flexible on location, **Travelodge Edinburgh Haymarket** ($70-120 per night) provides reasonable value in the Haymarket area with access to leisure facilities. This neighborhood sits west of the city center but has proper transport links and a more residential character than touristy zones.

## Budget Tips for Pool-Equipped Stays

**Book directly with hotels** rather than third-party sites. Most pool-equipped Edinburgh hotels offer loyalty discounts and will match rates if you call. Prestonfield and similar properties often have early-bird specials.

**Travel in shoulder seasons** (April-May or September-October). Pool-equipped hotels charge premium rates in summer, but you'll find 20-30% discounts in spring and fall when Edinburgh is genuinely pleasant without peak crowds.

**Consider longer stays.** Properties like Prestonfield offer weekly rates that work out 15-25% cheaper than nightly bookings. If you're spending five nights or more, always ask about extended-stay packages.

**Verify pool access beforehand.** Call the hotel directly and confirm whether the pool is indoor, heated, and year-round accessible. Online descriptions can be misleading about what "pool access" actually means.

## Neighborhoods Worth Knowing

**Morningside**, south of the city, feels leafy and residential. Several mid-range hotels here offer leisure facilities, though fewer have dedicated pools. It's quiet and walkable to Meadows Park but requires more travel time to Royal Mile attractions.

**The West End** (around Haymarket) offers good value and genuine local character. Hotels here serve business travelers and families, with straightforward amenities. It's quieter than city center but well-connected by bus.

**City Centre** hotels with pools are almost non-existent, so don't fixate on being directly on the Royal Mile. A short bus ride (5-10 minutes) to quieter neighborhoods often delivers better value and pool access simultaneously.

## Final Recommendations

Book **Prestonfield House** if budget allows—the experience justifies the cost. Choose **Murrayfield House** for the sweet spot between luxury, pool access, and reasonable pricing. For genuine budget consciousness, accept that you're trading on-site pools for leisurely facilities nearby, and opt for central hotels with partnerships to leisure centers.

Editing your expectations matters. Edinburgh's charm lies in its streets, architecture, and whisky bars—not resort-style amenities. Hotels with pools here serve a specific purpose: comfort and recovery. Choose one that fits your budget and location needs, then spend your real time exploring Scotland's capital.
